name: National Museum

text: Above the inner doors, in the stone: KEPT FOR EVERYONE. ENTRY FREE FOREVER.
Under it, smaller and newer: MAINTAINED WITH THE SUPPORT OF
THE MERIDIAN FOUNDATION. The museum's own name is the smaller of the two.
THE AURELIAN GALLERY. Nine rooms of a people who left no name for themselves.
What is known about them fills one card at the door.
What is guessed about them fills the other eight rooms.
Cases of resonance glass, cut and joined without heat.
Nobody in Averra can do this now. Three people have tried publicly
and one of them is a card in this case explaining what went wrong.
A wall of rubbings taken from Aurelian floors across the whole region.
The same spiral, the same circle, from the volcano to the wetlands.
One people, one language, one very long time, and then nothing at all.
The accession ledger, open, under glass, at a page in a small neat hand.
Most of this gallery was catalogued by one man over eleven years.
The page is signed E. of Hearthmere, and the ink has been touched up once.
A resonance ring, whole, on a stand, lit from below.
Struck, it is said to hold a note for a full minute.
The card asks you not to strike it. Somebody has, at some point, twice.
A second ring, broken in three, laid out as found.
The break is not weathering. Something pulled it apart from the inside.
FOUND: DROWNED SITE, EASTERN SHELF. NOT RECOVERED BY THIS MUSEUM.
THE HALL OF THE DELUGE. A painted panorama forty feet long,
and it takes a while to work out that the small pale marks in the water
are roofs.
The date of the Deluge, argued over in six panels by six scholars.
They agree on nothing except that it took less than a season
and that it was not the first thing that went wrong.
Cast and mounted: a whole Aurelian street, drowned and lifted, tile by tile.
The doors are all standing open. Every one of them.
The card is careful to say that this may mean nothing.
A case of what was found inside the houses. Bowls. Toys. A comb.
Nothing packed, nothing bundled, nothing hidden.
Whatever these people ran from, they did not know it was coming.
THE KIN GALLERY. Skeletons, casts and a hundred and eleven species,
with the ones nobody has seen alive in a lifetime marked in grey.
Eleven are grey. Two have been painted back in this year.
Under glass: an Aurelian carving of people and Kin, side by side,
and none of the Kin is on a lead, in a cage, or under anybody's hand.
The card calls this an artistic convention. The card may be wrong.
The largest object in the building: one vertebra, on its own trestle,
raised from the eastern shelf. It is taller than you are.
SPECIES UNKNOWN. NOT A WHALE. THAT IS ALL THAT CAN HONESTLY BE SAID.
The last case in the museum is empty, dusted, and labelled.
AURELIAN RESONANCE DEVICE, PORTABLE. ON LOAN.
The loan card gives a date eleven years old and no return date at all.

_plan: The museum is where Act 4 quietly hands the player the shape of the truth without anybody saying it: the Aurelian collection was catalogued by one man from Hearthmere over eleven years; a ring broken from the inside was recovered by somebody other than this museum; and the last case in the building is empty, on loan, eleven years, no return date. The Tideheart the player is carrying was accessioned here. Nobody in the building has made that connection, and neither has the museum.
